text:
anya (docs): FYI I opened a draft PR that consolidates examples for tiered rate/quota dashboards and SDK snippets. Link: https://git.internal/redwood/docs/pull/2410 :wave:

sam (eng-platform): Thank you. Quick check: the dashboard queries use token-normalized units. Are those per-minute or per-hour aggregates in your samples? We need to be explicit so billing and alerting match.

anya (docs): Right now I included both. I have an "hourly" example and a "1m moving" example. Each snippet is labeled.

mike (product): Nice. For external docs prefer hourly as the primary example (matches invoices). Keep the 1m variant as an "ops" snippet.

lia (devex): Heads-up: the sample JS SDK in the PR still used the old header X-Usage-Tokens. We migrated that to X-RW-Usage last sprint. Can we update the snippet?

anya (docs): Good catch. I'll update all examples to X-RW-Usage and add a note mapping the old header to the new one for people on older SDKs.

sam (eng-platform): Also add a Grafana panel link/reference. Panel id for the public consumption panel is 42. If you include a stable panel permalink that helps readers click through.

anya (docs): Will add permalink and panel id. Current curl example in PR:

```
# last hour, aggregated per minute
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \
  -H "X-RW-Usage: project=acme,env=prod" \
  "https://api.redwood.example/v1/usage?from=-1h&group_by=1m"
```

sam (eng-platform): Looks good. One more request: include a one-liner for canary -> stable migration so teams don't double-report to meters (we saw this during the rollout). Something like: "Ensure routing header is updated from tier=canary to tier=stable and that the meter_key is unique per route."

anya (docs): I'll add a troubleshooting callout: "If totals look doubled, verify routing headers and whether both canary and stable are emitting the same meter_key."

mike (product): Also please add a short blurb on burst credits and how they appear in the dashboard: customers ask whether "available" includes burst. Something concise: "Visible allocation = committed tier + burst; billing uses reconciled meter windows (UTC day)."

lia (devex): And add a small JS SDK demo for parsing hourly vs minute series so folks know how body.series[].points is arranged. Example I propose:

```
// hourly aggregation
const res = await fetch('/v1/usage?from=-1h&group_by=1h', {
  headers: { 'Authorization': `Bearer ${process.env.RW_KEY}`, 'X-RW-Usage': 'project=acme,env=prod' }
});
const body = await res.json();
console.log(body.series[0].points.map(p => p.value));
```

anya (docs): I'll include that under "SDK snippets" section and link to docs/units.md for the normalized token units.

sam (eng-platform): One more offtopic ask: add a short note about fallback model routing and meter attribution. If a request falls back to a cheaper model variant, the per-model meter can shift which confuses customers reconciling usage.

anya (docs): Good point. I'll add: "Fallback routing can change per-model attribution; use per-route snapshots to reconcile consumption per deployment."

mike (product): Looks good. After updates, tag me and sam for review. Also open a follow-up issue to add a small test prompt set that stresses token churn so Optimize can recommend batching/quantization. Not required to land this PR.

anya (docs): Will do. I pushed updates: header rename, JS snippet, Grafana panel link, hourly + 1m examples, burst credit callout, fallback routing note, and link to units.md. CI kicked off.

deploy-bot: docs-ci started for PR #2410  build 902 running.

sam (eng-platform): Thanks. I'll review after CI finishes.

anya (docs): CI passed, tagging reviewers @sam (eng-platform) @mike (product). :rocket:
